title: Lakeshore Brewing: governance and compliance before an IPO
judge_role: Founder and chief executive officer of LAKESHORE BREWING, a family company planning to list its shares on a U.S. stock exchange in 18 months

difficulty.rationale: Governance, independence and Sarbanes-Oxley before an IPO.

scenario:
You are to assume the role of controller of LAKESHORE BREWING, a family owned craft brewery. The founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of LAKESHORE BREWING (judge) has asked you to explain what the company must change before it becomes a public company.

LAKESHORE BREWING was started 25 years ago and now sells its beer in 12 states. To pay for a new brewery, the founder (judge) plans to list the company's shares on a U.S. stock exchange in 18 months. Investment bankers have told the founder (judge) that investors, the stock exchange and regulators will look closely at how the company is governed and controlled.

The founder (judge) has always made the major decisions personally and believes the current structure "has worked for 25 years." The founder (judge) asked you to review the company's current situation and to estimate the added costs of being a public company.

[Current governance and controls: see exhibits]

[Estimated first-year public company costs: see exhibits]

The founder (judge) wants a clear picture of what must change, why it matters and what it will cost, and also wants to know what employees throughout the company will be expected to do.

You must:
- Identify the factors that shape a company's governance structure
- Evaluate LAKESHORE BREWING's board and controls against public company expectations
- Explain how stronger governance will change decision making and management
- Explain the compliance requirements for financial reporting and internal control, and what a compliance program includes
- Explain each employee's role in meeting governance objectives

You will present your recommendations to the founder (judge) in a role-play to take place in the founder's office at the brewery. The founder (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented your recommendations and have answered the founder's (judge's) questions, the founder (judge) will conclude the role-play by thanking you for your work.
tasks: Identify the factors that shape a company's governance structure
Evaluate LAKESHORE BREWING's board and controls against public company expectations
Explain how stronger governance will change decision making and management
Explain the compliance requirements for financial reporting and internal control, and what a compliance program includes
Explain each employee's role in meeting governance objectives

exhibits.title: Current governance and controls
rows: 5 members: the CEO (founder); the chief financial officer (CFO); the founder's sister, who is vice president of marketing; the family attorney, whose law firm earns $80,000 a year from LAKESHORE; and a retired banker with no other ties to the company
The CFO approves his own expense reports
Reviewed (not audited) by a local CPA firm

judge_questions: The family attorney has been loyal for 20 years. Why can't he count as independent?

solution.overview: A strong answer identifies the factors that shape governance, shows that only 1 of 5 directors is independent and that the company lacks an audit committee, a code of conduct, a hotline and audited statements, and recommends specific fixes. The presenter explains Sarbanes-Oxley sections 302, 404 and 806 and the parts of a compliance program, totals first-year costs of $840,000, explains how decisions will become more checked and documented, and describes every employee's role.

answer: Ownership and size: a family company answers to a few owners; a public company answers to thousands of shareholders
Legal and listing requirements: SEC rules, the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and the stock exchange's listing standards
Industry regulation: federal and state alcohol licensing and tax rules
Investor expectations, the company's risk profile and its culture (tone at the top)

by_task.task: Evaluation of the board and controls
answer: Only 1 of 5 directors (the retired banker) is independent; the CEO, CFO and sister are insiders
The attorney is not independent because his firm earns $80,000 a year from LAKESHORE
Exchanges generally require a majority of independent directors and an audit committee made up entirely of independent directors, including a financial expert (phase-in periods apply to new listings)
Control gaps: the CFO approves his own expenses, there is no code of conduct or hotline, and statements are reviewed, not audited
Fixes: add independent directors; form audit, compensation and nominating committees; have the CEO or audit committee approve CFO expenses; adopt a code and hotline; move to audited statements

by_task.task: Effect on decision making and management
answer: The board, not the founder alone, approves major deals, budgets and executive pay
Decisions need more documentation, oversight and review, so they are slower but better checked
Management reports regularly to the board and its committees on results and risks
Independent directors bring outside views and protect all shareholders, not just the family
SOX section 302: the CEO and CFO personally certify each quarterly and annual report
SOX section 404: management assesses internal control over financial reporting each year; the outside auditor's attestation may be delayed for smaller or emerging growth companies
SOX section 806 protects whistleblowers from retaliation
A compliance program includes written policies, training, monitoring, reporting channels, discipline and periodic review
Follow the code of conduct and internal controls in daily work
Keep accurate, complete records and never override or work around a control
Complete required compliance and ethics training
Report concerns through the hotline or to a supervisor without fear of retaliation
Managers set the tone by modeling ethical behavior

calculations.label: Board independence
steps: Directors: CEO, CFO, founder's sister, family attorney, retired banker = 5
Not independent because of a business relationship: family attorney = 1
A majority would require at least 3 of 5 independent directors

judge_question_answers.question: The family attorney has been loyal for 20 years. Why can't he count as independent?
answer: Independence is about relationships, not loyalty or character
His firm earns $80,000 a year from LAKESHORE, so he has a financial reason to keep management happy
Exchange rules and investors look closely at business ties like this
He can remain as outside counsel and advise the board, but he cannot count as an independent director

judge_question_answers.question: Is the $840,000 worth it?
answer: The $840,000 is the price of access to public capital to fund the new brewery
Strong governance lowers the risk of fraud, restated financial statements and SEC penalties
Investors pay more for companies they trust, which can support a higher share price
The audit and internal audit also improve how the business is run, and some requirements phase in for smaller companies

key_concepts.definition: The system of rules, practices and oversight by which a company is directed and controlled for the benefit of its shareholders.
The group elected by shareholders to oversee management and approve major decisions.
A director with no employment, family or significant business ties to the company, so the director can judge management objectively.
A board committee of independent directors, including a financial expert, that oversees financial reporting, internal control and the outside auditor.
A 2002 federal law that set financial reporting and internal control requirements for public companies.
Requires the CEO and CFO to personally certify that each quarterly and annual report is accurate.
Requires management to assess internal control over financial reporting each year, with outside auditor attestation for larger companies.
Policies and procedures, such as approvals and separation of duties, that protect assets and make financial records reliable.
A confidential channel for employees to report suspected wrongdoing; SOX section 806 protects them from retaliation.
A company's system of policies, training, monitoring, reporting channels, discipline and review that keeps it within laws and rules.
A written statement of the ethical standards and behavior expected of every employee and director.
An audit gives reasonable assurance and an opinion on the financial statements; a review gives only limited assurance and is not enough for a public company.

notes: ICDC level because the student must evaluate board independence, connect specific Sarbanes-Oxley sections to the company's gaps and weigh costs against benefits for a founder who resists change. Watch for students who count the family attorney as independent, who confuse a review with an audit, or who describe governance only as rules instead of how decisions are made.

items.label: Ascertain employee's role in achieving governance objectives

criteria.exceeds: Explains that every employee must follow the code of conduct and internal controls, keep accurate records and never work around a control, complete compliance training and report concerns through the hotline without fear of retaliation, and that managers set the tone by modeling ethical behavior.
criteria.meets: Explains that employees must follow the code of conduct and controls, keep accurate records, complete training and report concerns through the hotline.
criteria.below: Mentions that employees should behave ethically but gives few specific responsibilities.
criteria.little: Does not address the employee's role, or says governance is only the board's job.

items.label: Identify the factors that impact governance structures

criteria.exceeds: Identifies ownership and size (a few family owners versus thousands of shareholders), legal and listing requirements (SEC rules, Sarbanes-Oxley, exchange standards), alcohol industry regulation, and investor expectations, risk profile and culture, and explains why the structure that "worked for 25 years" must change.
criteria.meets: Identifies at least ownership, legal and listing requirements, and industry regulation as factors shaping LAKESHORE's governance.
criteria.below: Names one or two factors in general terms without connecting them to LAKESHORE's move to public ownership.
criteria.little: Does not identify any factors that shape governance.

items.label: Describe the impact of governance processes on decision-making and management functions

criteria.exceeds: Shows only 1 of 5 directors (the retired banker) is independent, explains that the board, not the founder alone, will approve major deals, budgets and executive pay, and that decisions will be slower but better documented and checked, with management reporting regularly to board committees.
criteria.meets: Explains that the board will approve major decisions instead of the founder alone, with more documentation and oversight, and that the board needs more independent directors.
criteria.below: Describes governance only as rules without explaining how the founder's decision making will change.
criteria.little: Does not explain any effect on decision making, or says the founder can keep making decisions alone.

items.label: Comply with financial reporting and internal control regulations in accounting

criteria.exceeds: Explains SOX section 302 (CEO and CFO certify reports), 404 (management assesses internal control each year, with auditor attestation possibly delayed for smaller or emerging growth companies) and 806 (whistleblower protection), and fixes the gaps: an independent audit committee with a financial expert, CEO or audit committee approval of CFO expenses, and audited rather than reviewed statements.
criteria.meets: Explains SOX sections 302 and 404 and recommends an audit committee, stopping the CFO from approving his own expenses, and moving to audited statements.
criteria.below: Mentions Sarbanes-Oxley without explaining the sections, or confuses a review with an audit.
criteria.little: Does not address financial reporting or internal control requirements.

items.label: Discuss the nature and scope of compliance in the finance industry

criteria.exceeds: Describes a compliance program (written policies, training, monitoring, reporting channels, discipline and periodic review), adds a written code of conduct and hotline, totals first-year costs of $840,000 ($400,000 + $250,000 + $160,000 + $30,000), and weighs that cost against access to public capital.
criteria.meets: Describes the main parts of a compliance program and calculates first-year public company costs of $840,000.
criteria.below: Describes compliance vaguely, or miscalculates the costs (for example counting only one $80,000 director for a $760,000 total).
criteria.little: Does not discuss compliance or the costs.

items.label: Critical Thinking: Reason effectively and use systems thinking

criteria.exceeds: Connects board independence, internal controls, SOX requirements and employee behavior into one governance system that investors and regulators will judge before the IPO.
criteria.meets: Reasons correctly from the exhibits to the gaps LAKESHORE must fix.
criteria.below: Lists gaps without showing why they matter, or misses key gaps such as the attorney's $80,000 business tie.

items.label: Problem Solving: Make judgments and decisions and solve problems

criteria.exceeds: Gives the founder a clear action list for the 18 months: add independent directors, form audit, compensation and nominating committees, fix CFO expense approval, adopt a code and hotline, and move to audited statements.
criteria.meets: Makes clear recommendations to fix the board and the main control gaps.
criteria.below: Gives recommendations that are partly correct or not clearly stated.
criteria.little: Makes no recommendation, or agrees the current structure is fine.

criteria.exceeds: Explains governance and SOX in plain language and respectfully persuades a founder who resists change, with confident and professional delivery.
criteria.meets: Presents the gaps, requirements and costs clearly and in an organized way.
criteria.below: Presentation is hard to follow, relies on jargon, or skips steps.

items.label: Creativity and Innovation: Show evidence of creativity

criteria.exceeds: Uses a simple visual such as a current versus required table for the board and controls, or a timeline of changes over the 18 months before listing.
criteria.meets: Organizes the recommendations in a way that makes them easy to understand.
criteria.below: Presents the facts with little effort to make them engaging or easy to follow.
criteria.little: Shows no evidence of creativity or original thought.

items.label: Overall impression and responses to the judge's questions

criteria.exceeds: Answers both questions confidently: independence is about relationships, not loyalty, and the attorney's firm earns $80,000 a year from LAKESHORE, though he can stay on as outside counsel; and the $840,000 is the price of public capital for the new brewery, lowers the risk of fraud, restatements and SEC penalties, and builds investor trust.
criteria.meets: Answers both questions mostly correctly, including the attorney's $80,000 business tie and why the $840,000 is worth paying.
criteria.below: Answers only one question correctly, or gives vague answers.
criteria.little: Cannot answer the judge's questions, or agrees the attorney counts as independent.

key_points: Governance is shaped by ownership and size, SEC and exchange rules, Sarbanes-Oxley, alcohol regulation, investor expectations and culture
Only 1 of 5 directors (the retired banker) is independent; the attorney is not because his firm earns $80,000 a year from LAKESHORE
Add independent directors and form an audit committee of independent directors with a financial expert
Fix control gaps: the CFO approving his own expenses, no code of conduct, no hotline, and reviewed rather than audited statements
SOX 302 (CEO and CFO certify reports), 404 (internal control assessment) and 806 (whistleblower protection)
Every employee follows the code and controls, keeps accurate records, completes training and reports concerns
